canonical_task: computable in P by ordered DFS
citation: Reif, Depth-first search is inherently sequential, Inf. Proc. Lett. 20 (1985)

canonical_task: GEN is P-complete (canonical monotone-closure problem)
citation: Jones & Laaser (1976); GHR (1995)

canonical_task: CA t-step prediction is P-complete
citation: Greenlaw, Hoover & Ruzzo, Limits to Parallel Computation: P-Completeness Theory (1995)

canonical_task: plane-sweep triangulation is P-complete
citation: Atallah-Callahan-Goodrich (1993); GHR (1995)

canonical_task: greedy first-fit coloring, poly-time
k-Colorability decision (chi(G) <= k)
citation: Karp, Reducibility among combinatorial problems, in Complexity of Computer Computations (1972) 85-103
note: one of Karp's 21; 3-COL (graph-3-coloring) is the k=3 restriction, a separate row (S2)

canonical_task: axial 3-index assignment decision: a set of n disjoint triples of total cost <= B?
citation: Garey & Johnson, Computers and Intractability (1979) [3-Dimensional Matching, SP1]; via Karp, Reducibility among combinatorial problems (1972)
note: NP-hardness by 3-Dimensional Matching (feasibility); the min-cost assignment generalizes it. Distinct from 3-dimensional matching (feasibility) and the planar 3-index assignment (S2)

canonical_task: Balanced Connected q-Partition decision: a connected q-partition with min part-weight >= B?
citation: Dyer & Frieze, On the complexity of partitioning graphs into connected subgraphs, Discrete Appl. Math. 10 (1985) 139-153
note: NP-complete (strongly NP-hard, even on q-connected graphs). Distinct from graph bisection / edge-cut partitioning (S2)

canonical_task: Capacitated Facility Location decision: a feasible open-set + assignment of total cost <= B?
citation: generalizes metric Uncapacitated Facility Location, NP-hard via Set Cover (Cornuejols, Nemhauser & Wolsey 1990); Garey & Johnson 1979
note: NP-hard (contains metric UFL). Distinct from uncapacitated facility location and from k-median (S2)

canonical_task: Constrained Shortest Path decision: an s-t path of cost <= C and resource <= R?
citation: Garey & Johnson, Computers and Intractability (1979) [Shortest Weight-Constrained Path, ND30]
note: NP-complete (weakly — pseudo-polynomial by DP over the budget). Distinct from ordinary shortest path (poly-time) (S2)

canonical_task: Euclidean TSP decision: a tour of length <= L?
citation: Papadimitriou, The Euclidean traveling salesman problem is NP-complete, Theoret. Comput. Sci. 4 (1977) 237-244
note: NP-hard (Papadimitriou 1977). Distinct from metric TSP (general metric) and general (non-metric) TSP (S2)

canonical_task: unit-disk cover decision: cover P with <= k unit disks? NP-complete
citation: Fowler, Paterson & Tanimoto, Optimal packing and covering in the plane are NP-complete, Information Processing Letters 12 (1981) 133-137

canonical_task: Harmonious Colouring decision: harmonious colouring with <= k colours? NP-complete (also NP-complete on trees)
citation: Hopcroft & Krishnamoorthy, On the harmonious coloring of graphs, SIAM Journal on Algebraic and Discrete Methods 4 (1983) 306-311

canonical_task: List Colouring decision: proper colouring respecting the lists? NP-complete (k-colouring is the all-lists={1..k} case)
citation: Karp, Reducibility among combinatorial problems, in Complexity of Computer Computations (1972) 85-103
note: generalizes 3-colouring (a Karp NP-complete problem); NP-complete a fortiori

canonical_task: Maximum Induced Matching decision: induced matching of size >= k? NP-complete (even on bipartite graphs)
citation: Stockmeyer & Vazirani, NP-completeness of some generalizations of the maximum matching problem, Information Processing Letters 15 (1982) 14-19

canonical_task: Min-Sum Set Cover decision: an ordering of total cover time <= B?
citation: Feige, Lovász & Tetali, Approximating min sum set cover, Algorithmica 40 (2004) 219-234

canonical_task: Minimum k-Cut decision (k part of input): edges of total weight <= W whose removal gives >= k components?
citation: Goldschmidt & Hochbaum, A polynomial algorithm for the k-cut problem for fixed k, Math. Oper. Res. 19 (1994) 24-37
note: NP-hard when k is part of the input; polynomial (n^O(k^2)) for every FIXED k

canonical_task: d-Dimensional Knapsack decision: a feasible subset of profit >= P?
citation: Garey & Johnson, Computers and Intractability (1979) [Knapsack, MP9]
note: NP-hard (contains 0/1 Knapsack, d=1); strongly NP-hard for d part of the input (Chekuri-Khanna)

canonical_task: Planar 3-SAT: is the planar 3-CNF formula satisfiable?
citation: Lichtenstein, Planar formulae and their uses, SIAM J. Comput. 11 (1982) 329-343
note: NP-complete (Lichtenstein 1982); the workhorse starting point for planar NP-hardness reductions

canonical_task: QKP decision: total quadratic profit >= V within capacity?
citation: Gallo, Hammer & Simeone, Quadratic knapsack problems, Math. Programming Study 12 (1980) 132-149

canonical_task: Roman Domination decision: Roman dominating function of weight <= k?
citation: Cockayne, Dreyer, Hedetniemi & Hedetniemi, Roman domination in graphs, Discrete Math. 278 (2004) 11-22

canonical_task: Stacker Crane decision: a tour serving all arcs of length <= B?
citation: Frederickson, Hecht & Kim, Approximation algorithms for some routing problems, SIAM J. Comput. 7 (1978) 178-193
note: generalizes metric TSP (a degenerate arc set)

canonical_task: Total Dominating Set decision: total dominating set of size <= k?
citation: Laskar, Pfaff, Hedetniemi & Hedetniemi, On the algorithmic complexity of total domination, SIAM J. Alg. Disc. Meth. 5 (1984) 420-425

canonical_task: Vector Bin Packing decision: pack into <= k bins?
citation: Garey, Graham, Johnson & Yao, Resource constrained scheduling as generalized bin packing, JCTA 21 (1976) 257-298

canonical_task: existence of a linear extension: every finite poset has one (order-extension principle); a witness is produced by topological sort in linear time — the decoupling witness
citation: Szpilrajn, Sur l'extension de l'ordre partiel, Fund. Math. 16 (1930) 386-389
note: every partial order extends to a total order (Szpilrajn 1930); constructive by topological sort. Existence is trivial
